findings.claim: The text of the First Amendment prohibits Congress from making laws abridging freedom of speech.
findings.reason: The excerpt transcribes the First Amendment as saying Congress shall make no law abridging freedom of speech.

evidence.text:
Note: This is a transcription of the enrolled original of Congress’s joint resolution proposing the Bill of Rights; spelling and punctuation reflect the original. On September 25, 1789, the First Congress proposed 12 amendments. Ten were ratified on December 15, 1791, as the first ten amendments. The proposed Article 2 was ratified in 1992 as the 27th Amendment; Article 1 was never ratified.

Amendment I: Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof; or abridging freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.

Amendment II: A well

findings.claim: The First Amendment requires Congress to license every newspaper before publication.
findings.reason: The excerpt says Congress shall make no law abridging freedom of speech or of the press; it does not require licensing newspapers before publication.

findings.claim: The 2024 edition of Georgia Code section 9-3-32 states a four-year period after accrual for recovery of personal property or damages for its conversion or destruction.
findings.reason: The excerpt identifies the 2024 Georgia Code and states that the covered actions must be brought within four years after the right of action accrues.

evidence.text:
2024 Georgia Code § 9-3-32 — Accrual of actions for recovery of personal property or loss of timber; damages for conversion or destruction

Actions to recover personal property, or for damages for its conversion or destruction, must be brought within four years after the right of action accrues. Actions involving unauthorized cutting, or cutting and carrying away, of timber from another’s property must be brought within four years after the cutting or cutting and carrying away.

The section states it was amended by 2014 Ga. Laws 619, § 1, effective July 1, 2014. The page identifies itself as the 2024 Code and notes that a newer version is available.

findings.claim: The 2024 edition of Georgia Code section 9-3-32 states a one-year period after accrual for recovery of personal property or damages for its conversion or destruction.
findings.reason: The 2024 Code excerpt states a four-year period after accrual, not a one-year period.
